agents.reasoning: Primary-document build. The Q3 2026 10-Q, release and transcript give actuals (room nights 345M +7%, gross bookings $54.5B +10%, adjusted revenue $9.79B, take rate -15 bp) and the Q4 guide (room nights 1-3%, adjusted revenue 0-2%, EBITDA about flat). The $900M FTC revenue reduction plus a $100M accrual is booked as a one-off and an equity adjustment. The record: annual first revenue guides were beaten in FY2024 (+3.4% vs mid) and FY2025 (+8.0%), but FY2026's first guide (low double digits) is now a ~3% miss, so I give no beat premium. Drivers: room nights from global travel demand (UN Tourism 2026 cut to +1-2%) plus a share-gain spread narrowed from ~4.5 pts to ~2 for AI and competition; ADR +3% (CFO); take rate down 10 bp/yr on flights mix; marketing flat as a share of GB; non-marketing opex +6.6% net of the $650M transformation run-rate. FY2027 revenue is $31.4B (consensus $31.5B, StockAnalysis 2026-11-13) and EPS ~$11.7 (consensus adjusted $12.23, ~4% below). Buybacks of ~$9B/yr cut shares 6.5%/yr. Valuation: P/E on horizon NTM EPS, exit 14.6x from the k = 0.8 shrink of 13.1x toward the 22.5x two-peer median, giving a research target (12m) of $184.82 (+17%). The downside (P10, $123) and upside (P90, $243) move room nights, take rate and marketing and ±3 turns of multiple; the left tail is fatter, consistent with 39% realized volatility. The room-night spread is the biggest judgment call (±7-10%), flagged for Kilian. Research was limited: numeric Q2/Q3 2026 quarter guides and a 2027 UN Tourism forecast were not found, and the SEC refused direct curl (filings read via WebFetch and the cached companyfacts).

agents.reasoning: Facts: Q3 2026 beat its own guide on every line (room nights +7%, adjusted revenue +9%, adj. EBITDA +9%; GAAP revenue -1% after a $900M FTC revenue reduction; src 1,3). But the CFO guided Q4 to room nights +1-3% and adjusted revenue +0-2%, citing October Middle East and European disruption (src 3). Industry lane: Expedia guided Q4 bookings down from +11% to +3-5% and fell 12%, with its CFO naming the same geopolitical headwinds (src 10,11,12). Airbnb accelerated (src 13), which shows that share in alternative accommodations is contested. UN Tourism cut 2026 arrivals growth to 1-2% (src 14,15). U.S. hotel ADR/RevPAR were firm in late October (src 25), and CoStar raised its 2026-27 outlook (src 16). AI agents: Google's partner list runs through the OTAs (src 18), but Meta Muse direct-booking fears hit the group in September (src 19,24). BKNG says LLM referrals are <1% of room nights (CFO, src 3). Build: four quarterly drivers. Room nights +2.5% in Q4 (inside the guide, below the record-adjusted 297.7M) and +5% in 2027-28. GB per room night +1-3%. Take rate -10 bp in 2027 on flight mix. GAAP margin +30 bp a year from transformation savings net of investment. FY2027 revenue $31.0B (1.5% below the $31.5B consensus) and GAAP EPS $11.67 (4.6% below the $12.23 adjusted consensus, src 9): moderately conservative per rule 0c. Value: one P/E leg; the exit 14.3x comes from the k = 0.8 shrink of the own 13.1x toward the 2-peer median of 22.5x, less 0.3x for regulation. Research target (12m) $180.89 (+14.8%). Downside P10 $116 (volume, take and margin cuts plus de-rating to ~11x) and upside P90 $234 give a fatter left tail, consistent with 39% realized vol and AI-disintermediation risk. Research was limited to web sources; the SEC blocked direct curl, so filings were read via WebFetch and companyfacts.

Litigation stack: EU hotel parity collective action (18,135 hotels, several billion euros, hearings 2027), Dutch consumer claims EUR 965M (jurisdiction upheld 2026-10-28), Spain EUR 413M fine under appeal. AI: Google moved agentic hotel booking into AI Mode in the US (Skift 2026-08-27) with Booking as a partner; LLM referrals are <1% of room nights (CFO). Sell-side mostly Buy but cutting (Wells Fargo EW $190; Feb 2026 cuts up to 23% on AI fears); Morgan Stanley sees AI as a channel and online travel +7% a year. Build: quarterly drivers (room nights, $/room night, take rate, marketing % bookings, fixed costs) calibrated to the supplements; FY2027 revenue $30,987M (-1.6% vs MarketScreener consensus $31,505M), EBIT $10,642M (-4.7% vs $11,162M), EPS ~$11.5 (-3% vs $11.85); NTM EPS at the horizon ~$12.2 vs consensus ~$13.5 (-10%: we have no share gains, continued take-rate dilution and +5% fixed costs). Valued at 14.2x (k-rule on a 2-peer median, less 0.75 turn AI risk) minus probability-weighted litigation. Downside/upside move the drivers and the multiple to genuine 1-in-10 cases; left tail fatter. Sources: 12 of 23 in lane; of the 16 non-company-filing/transcript sources, 12 (75%) are lane kinds (litigation, regulatory, critical press, target cuts, AI-threat trade press). Research limits: Nasdaq/Zacks consensus API not reachable (blocked), Twelve Data estimates need a higher plan; FY2027 consensus taken from MarketScreener.

agents.reasoning: Started from the Q3 2026 release and corrected call (src 2, 3): room nights +7%, GB +10%, adjusted revenue +9% but GAAP revenue -1% on a $900M FTC revenue reduction (plus $100M G&A accrual), and a Q4 guide of room nights +1-3%, adjusted revenue 0-2%, EBITDA about flat as the US-Iran war (Manifold src 14) and October disruptions bite. BKNG has beaten its quarterly revenue guide 4 of 4 times by a median 3.3% vs the midpoint, but the first FY2026 guide (low double digits) was cut to high single digits; I set Q4 from a two-year-stack volume build (+3%) and a guided take-rate gap, landing above the revenue range and inside the room-night range. Alternative-lane evidence: Similarweb October visits -8% m/m (seasonal) with affiliate the largest desktop channel (src 11); app trackers noisy (AltIndex inconsistent, src 12; Apptopia MAU +11% y/y in Q4 2025, src 13); LLM referrals <1% of room nights (CFO) while Meta's Muse launched with Expedia and topped the App Store (src 21), the biggest unpriced-by-sell-side risk; newsletters (StrataFinance, FourWeekMBA, Skift/Hospitality.today) frame BKNG growth as share-capture rather than demand, which argues against mapping Tourism Economics' +8% 2027 arrivals one-for-one, so FY2027 room nights +5.9%. Prediction markets on the Iran war are thin or resolved and enter only as context. Valuation: peers are only EXPE and ABNB (Trip.com/MakeMyTrip excluded by rule, UBER off-model); BKNG at 13.1x NTM consensus vs a 22.5x peer median; k = 0.8 gives 14.6x on our ~$12.94 NTM EPS = $189 (+20%). Downside P10 $130 (room nights -4%, take -20 bp, marketing +10 bp, -3 turns) and upside P90 $233 (+2.5% volume, -5 bp marketing, +2.5 turns): a fatter left tail, consistent with 39% realized vol. Research was limited by sec.gov refusing the scripted User-Agent for some pages (read via WebFetch/relays) and X being unreachable; the FY2025 first annual guide was not re-read. Flags: horizon P/E alternatives (own multiple held, -10%) exceed 5%; 2-peer set; Q4 above guide.

inputs_detail.derivation: Actuals from releases (Q1 FY2025-Q3 FY2026). Q4 FY2026 = 285 x 1.035 (guide 1-3% by CFO Steenbergen; record +2.7% on levels; trimmed for October Middle East hit and Expedia's Q4 slowdown). FY2027 quarters y/y +4.5/5.5/4.5/5.5% (tough Q1/Q3 comps after +6.0%/+6.8%; easy Q2 after the Middle East hit and Q4 after +3.5%); FY2028 +5%. Real-world case: global travel grows GDP+1-2pts (CEO Fogel, JPM conf.), ~4-5% a year, plus Booking share gain; in 2026 Booking room nights grew 6.0% YTD vs UN Tourism's 1-2% arrivals forecast, i.e. ~4pts of outgrowth in a weak year; we take ~1pt less outgrowth than 2026 as AI channels and Middle East persist. Alternatives: (a) guide-record path ~+4.75% Q4 and 6% 2027; (b) consensus 2027 revenue +10.6% GAAP (~+7.9% ex-FTC) implying ~6% RN; (c) UN Tourism 1-2% + 2026 outgrowth 4.5pts = 5.5-6.5%.

agents.reasoning: Base rates first: Booking has beaten 4 of its last 5 room-night guides (median +2.7% on levels) and all 5 revenue and EBITDA guides (median +3.0% and +5.8%), but its first FY2026 annual guide ('low double digits' revenue, mid-teens EPS) was cut to high single digits, so the beat habit is quarterly sandbagging, not annual. The Q4 FY2026 guide (RN +1-3%) is the weakest in years; Expedia's Q4 bookings guide (+3.3-5.2% after +11%) and UN Tourism's cut to 1-2% arrivals growth show an industry slowdown from the Middle East conflict and airfares, not a Booking-specific break. Macro odds: Kalshi prices a 2027 US recession at ~21.5%; Polymarket's 2026 market is ~2% (oddpool's 37% looks stale). Valuation history: the stock sits at ~13x NTM consensus EPS, below its decade forward-P/E lows of 15-16x (eToro) and a TTM ~16x vs a 5-year median ~29x (VCP Scanner), after a ~34% peak-to-trough drawdown (TIKR) and -20% over a year. Model: quarterly room nights x GB/RN x take, margins from the adjusted EBITDA margin with a +0.3pt/yr step from the $650M savings net of investment; FY2027 revenue ~1pt below consensus ex-FTC; our FY2027 EPS is ~$11.5 vs StockAnalysis $12.23 (-6%): about 1pt from revenue, ~2pts from net interest at the 8.5% Q3 run-rate on net debt that rises as returns run at 30% of revenue, ~2pts from buybacks at -5% a year vs the -7.5% Q3 pace, and the rest from a margin step (+0.3pt) below the +0.5pt FY2026 plan. Horizon P/E per the k=0.8 rule on a 2-peer median, EV/EBITDA cross-check. Downside (P10) combines recession-type volumes with a de-rating to ~11x; upside (P90) a guide beat plus partial re-rating to ~17.6x. Research limited: SEC EDGAR refused the generic curl agent, so filings were read with WebFetch; X/Twitter not tried.
